timeline.title: Jensen Huang Expresses Willingness to Return as Nvidia CEO After Resignation
timeline.summary: Jensen Huang has stated he would be 'honored' to return as CEO of Nvidia if asked by the board. His comments follow his recent resignation amid reports of personal scandals, including affairs with an employee and a woman linked to Chinese intelligence. Huang's potential reinstatement has garnered significant support, including a petition signed by 190,000 people, many of whom are Nvidia employees.
key_facts: Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia last week.
He expressed willingness to return if the board requests it.
A petition for his reinstatement has over 190,000 signatures.

timeline.title: Jensen Huang Returns as Nvidia CEO Following Controversial Resignation
timeline.summary: Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as its President and CEO, just days after he resigned amid allegations of extramarital affairs and connections to a Chinese intelligence asset. The board's decision, influenced by advocacy from US President Donald Trump, has led to a significant surge in Nvidia's stock price. Huang's return has sparked discussions about potential investigations into the circumstances surrounding his resignation.
key_facts: Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO of Nvidia after a brief resignation.
His resignation was linked to allegations of affairs and espionage concerns.
US President Donald Trump advocated for Huang's return to the board.
Nvidia's stock surged 32% following the announcement.

event_overview.title: About Nvidia Leadership
event_overview.subject: Nvidia Leadership
event_overview.summary: This event concerns a brief 2026 leadership transition at NVIDIA, the Delaware-incorporated, Santa Clara-based technology company. Jensen Huang resigned as president, chief executive officer and board member in November; the board appointed CFO Colette Kress interim CEO, then reinstated Huang shortly afterward while an independent board investigation and new compliance measures continued.

facts.label: Leadership transition dates
facts.value: NVIDIA's board accepted Huang's resignation effective November 11, 2026. The board reinstated him as president, CEO and director effective November 22, 2026; the company announced the action on November 23.

facts.label: Interim management
facts.value: Following the resignation, the board named Colette M. Kress—NVIDIA's executive vice president and CFO since 2013—as interim CEO while it began a search for a permanent successor. After Huang's reinstatement, Kress continued as executive vice president and CFO.

facts.label: Board governance
facts.value: Harvey C. Jones was appointed chair of NVIDIA's board during the transition and remained chair after Huang's reinstatement. NVIDIA's board is the corporate body that made the executive appointments and reinstatement decisions.

facts.label: Investigation and compliance response
facts.value: The independent directors opened an investigation after reporting that Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort; NVIDIA said it had no reason at that point to believe national security or company secrets had been compromised. The company said the investigation would continue after his reinstatement and announced a board National Security and Export Control Committee plus a planned chief compliance o

facts.label: Company context
facts.value: NVIDIA is incorporated in Delaware and has its principal executive offices in Santa Clara, California. Huang founded the company in 1993 and had served as its president, CEO and a director since its inception before the November 2026 transition.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the resignation, public discussion of a possible return, and Huang's reinstatement in November 2026; it does not attempt to chronicle NVIDIA's broader business performance, all investigation details, or every reaction to the leadership changes.
